source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Front Suspension, p.3-3

procedures.title: Front wheel bearings: adjust
steps: Raise the wheel; take off the hub cap and the dust cap, then pull the cotter pin from the spindle end.
Turn the wheel by hand while tightening the spindle nut to 12 lb-ft.
Back the nut off one flat and fit the cotter pin; if the slot and hole do not align, back off a further 1/2 flat or less until the pin fits.
Spin the wheel to confirm it turns freely, then spread and bend the cotter pin end to lock it.
Refit the dust cap and hub cap (or wheel disc) and lower the wheel.
Repeat on the other front wheel.
notes: Badly adjusted bearings cause poor steering stability: wander, shimmy and rapid tire wear.
The spindle is drilled both ways and the nut is slotted on all six sides, which allows fine adjustment.
Do not repack or adjust wheel bearings as part of new car conditioning.

procedures.title: Front end alignment: preliminary checks
steps: Follow the instructions supplied with the alignment machine being used.
Check alignment with the car level and at curb weight.

Before aligning, look for and fix: a loose or misadjusted steering gear; a steering gear housing loose on the frame; worn or loose spherical joints or steering shaft coupling; loose tie rods or steering connections; wrong front spring heights; out-of-balance or low tires; misadjusted wheel bearings; faulty shock absorbers.
Roll the car forward before measuring so slack is taken up as in forward driving.
notes: Steering complaints are not always caused by alignment, hence the checks first.
